ai.title: Add retry logic for diff block generation
ai.summary: Added a retry mechanism in `backend/src/prompts.ts` for diff block generation. If `parseAndGetDiffBlocks` detects `<old>` content that fails to match the file via strict string inclusion, the system constructs a corrective prompt containing the failed blocks and requests a new strategy from Claude. This handles cases where the model generates valid but non-applicable diff blocks.

eli5.text: When you ask the system to make a set of edits to a file, it now double-checks whether the specific text it planned to replace actually exists in the file. If some edits don't line up, instead of failing silently or applying a partial change, the system sends those failed edits back with a fresh explanation of what the final result should look like and asks for a corrected version, then applies that second attempt. You would notice this as fewer cases where an intended change simply doesn't appear in the file because the original snippet couldn't be found. This is live today for any edit processed through the diff-generation path.

ai.title: Add STOPMARKER instruction to Claude prompt loop
ai.summary: Added explicit instruction to end responses with STOP_MARKER in promptClaudeAndGetFileChanges. Updated knowledge file instruction to allow editing existing files rather than just adding notes. Added duplicate debug logging for message count.

eli5.text: When the assistant is working through a task step-by-step, it now has a new reminder to stop typing once it's finished, so it doesn't keep going on and on. At the same time, it now knows it's okay to update an existing notes file when it learns something new, instead of only creating a brand new one. You wouldn't directly notice this while using the app, since it's an internal tweak to how the assistant behaves behind the scenes.

ai.title: Fix deprecated ts-jest globals warning
ai.summary: Removed deprecated `globals` config for `ts-jest` in `backend/jest.config.js`, migrating `tsconfig` path to the `transform` array syntax. Updated `testMatch` patterns to strictly target `.test.ts` files. Added `test:coverage` script to `backend/package.json`.

eli5.text: If you run the test suite for the backend (the part of the system that runs on the server), you should no longer see a loud yellow warning about a deprecated setting that tells ts-jest to use 'globals'. The system now uses the newer, recommended way to set the same options, and it tightened up which test files get run so they must be named *.test.ts. A new script was also added so you can generate test coverage reports with a single command.

ai.title: Add tricky diff blocks test
ai.summary: Added a test case to `prompts.test.ts` to verify `generateDiffBlocks` handles complex indentation changes. Introduced mock data files `index-old.ts` and `index-new.ts` in `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__` to serve as the test fixtures.

eli5.text: The system now includes a new test that checks whether the assistant correctly updates code when lines shift due to changing indentation (like when code blocks move in or out of functions). The test uses two example files showing a before-and-after version of a script, and it verifies that every change is applied accurately so the final result matches the updated file. Since it is a test, you will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves today, but it helps ensure future code updates handle tricky formatting changes without breaking.

ai.title: Rename old/new diff tags to search/replace
ai.summary: backend/src/prompts.ts renames <old>/<new> XML tags to <search>/<replace> in Claude prompts and diff parsing. Internal variable names (oldContent, newContent) updated to searchContent, replaceContent to match the new schema. The string replacement logic in processFileBlock and generateDiffBlocks now expects the new tag names for exact matches. No external API changes; purely internal prompt engineering and code consistency.

eli5.text: The AI helper that edits your files now talks about changes using the words 'search' and 'replace' instead of 'old' and 'new'. This is something only the people who build and fix the editing system will notice if they look closely; there's no change to how the editing actually works or what you see. It's a behind-the-scenes cleanup to keep the instructions and code consistent, and it's already live.

ai.title: prompts.ts: lettered edit groups + indentation retry fallback
ai.summary: Prompt steps 2/3/5 now require lettered edit groups (A, B...) with per-edit context and indentation levels, and example search/replace blocks are prefixed with those letters. parseAndGetDiffBlocks gains a tryToDoStringReplacementWithExtraIndentation fallback: when a search block misses, it retries by prefixing every line with 1-12 spaces then 1-6 tabs to recover from model indentation drift. Covers backend prompts.ts plus updated prompts.test.ts and index-new-goal.ts mock data. Fallback returns the indented search/replace pair only on exact match, otherwise the block still falls through to diffBlocksThatDidntMatch.

eli5.text: When the coding assistant writes instructions for making a code change, its prompts now have to ask for labeled, lettered groups (A, B, etc.) for each separate edit, along with the right indentation details for each part. If the system can't find an exact match for a requested change because of spacing issues, it will retry by adding extra spaces and tabs (up to a point) so the edit can still apply. If a perfect match still can't be found after that, the change falls back to being reported as unmatched rather than silently failing.

ai.title: Add existing-comments test fixtures and reorganize mock data
ai.summary: New test fixtures under `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/existing-comments/` validate diff generation when preserving existing comments. Previous indentation-specific mock files moved to `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/indentation/` for clearer categorization. `prompts.test.ts` updated to reference new paths and includes a test case for handling lots of comments.

eli5.text: Your coding assistant now does a better job when you ask it to edit code that already contains comments. It can now reliably preserve those existing comments while making changes, instead of accidentally dropping or breaking them. The team added new example files that specifically test this comment-handling behavior, and they reorganized where example files live so related pieces are easier to find.

ai.title: Add chat history menu to manicode mock data
ai.summary: Added interactive chat history menu to `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/existing-comments` scripts. Implemented `displayMenu` and `initializeMenu` functions for navigating chat sessions with arrow keys. Constants `CHATS_PER_PAGE` and `NEW_CHAT_OPTION` moved into function scope. Scope limited to test mock data files; no production code affected.

eli5.text: If you opened this program's test environment and started typing, you can now press a key to open a menu showing your previous conversations, which appear as a tidy list you can scroll through with the arrow keys, with the option to start a fresh conversation at the top. This works in both the old and new versions of the test setup files, but since it only affects those internal mock files used for development, you won't see any difference in your normal use of the software.

ai.title: Add unsure and scope guardrails to system prompt
ai.summary: Added explicit instructions to `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` requiring the agent to state uncertainty and defer on large scopes. The prompt now mandates the phrase "I don't have enough information to confidently answer your question" when unsure. It also instructs the agent to identify requests exceeding 750 lines of code as too large and ask the user to select a sub-problem. This internal change applies to the backend system prompt generation.

eli5.text: The assistant that helps with coding projects now has clearer instructions about when it should admit uncertainty and when a request is too big to handle all at once. If you ask it something it's not confident about, it's been told to say so directly using a specific phrase. If you ask for a change that would require writing more than 750 lines of code, it's been instructed to tell you the scope is too large and ask you to pick a smaller piece to work on first. These rules were added to the assistant's main set of instructions, making those responses part of how it behaves starting today.

ai.title: System prompt adds step-by-step plan reasoning
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts injects an instruction for Manny to explain plan reasoning step-by-step for complex tasks and re-explain after error corrections. The change also adds a 'You are concise' directive to the persona block. Scope is limited to the backend system prompt generation logic.

eli5.text: When you ask Manny to do something complex, the instructions that guide Manny now tell it to spell out, step by step, why it's choosing each part of its plan. This only affects the internal guidance that shapes how Manny thinks through and explains its work, not anything you see directly. If you could read that guidance, you'd see a new line telling Manny to first lay out the plan, then walk through the reasoning behind each step, and after fixing a mistake to re-explain the reasoning for the corrected plan.

ai.title: Chat history menu in CLI
ai.summary: Added interactive chat history navigation menu to CLI input handling in `src/index.ts`. Pressing ESC now toggles a paginated list of previous chats and a 'New chat' option, selectable via arrow keys and SPACE/ENTER. This replaces the previous behavior where ESC immediately exited the application when not receiving a response. The menu logic manages state via `isInMenu`, `menuSelectedIndex`, and `menuOffset`, integrating with `chatStorage.listChats()`.

eli5.text: When you press the Escape key in the terminal, instead of immediately quitting the program, it now shows a list of your previous conversations that you can scroll through with the arrow keys. You can pick an old chat to jump back into, or choose a "New chat" option to start fresh, and pressing Escape a second time while in this list will exit the program. The change applies to everyone using the command-line version of the assistant, and it adds a small, interactive menu that appears whenever you press Escape outside of an active response.

ai.title: Fix diff application bug and improve prompts
ai.summary: Corrects `processFileBlock` to record actual `searchContent`/`replaceContent` instead of original `oldContent`/`newContent`. Refines file-editing prompts to enforce exact context matching, remove invalid placeholder comments from search blocks, and simplify indentation instructions. Adds temporary `fs.writeFileSync` debug hook in `backend/src/prompts.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant edits a file, it now records the actual changes it made rather than the original text it intended to change, fixing a mismatch in the change history. The instructions given to the assistant were tightened so it provides exact matching text instead of placeholder comments, and the way indentation instructions are written was simplified. A small amount of temporary code was added to help debug file editing, and these edits are already live in the backend.

ai.title: Standardize prompt shorthand to // ... existing code ...
ai.summary: Backend prompts in `backend/src/prompts.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` now strictly enforce `// ... existing code ...` as the sole shorthand for unchanged code, removing support for `... rest of the file` and similar variations. This standardization ensures consistent parsing of search/replace blocks by eliminating ambiguous placeholder formats. The change affects the core editing instructions sent to the model, requiring all file modification examples to use the single approved comment string.

eli5.text: The assistant's editing instructions now use one consistent way to show where existing code should stay when showing how to change a file. Instead of allowing shorthand like '... rest of the file', only the comment '//... existing code...' is recognized as the placeholder for unchanged code. This affects the internal prompts that guide how code edits are described, so any examples of modifying files must follow this single format. You wouldn't see this directly, but if you reviewed the editing guidelines given to the assistant, you'd notice the simplified and uniform placeholder rule.

ai.title: Robust backspace handling for multi-line input
ai.summary: Implemented dynamic line tracking and clearing logic in refreshLine to support multi-line input rendering. Replaced simple clearLine with cursor movement loops based on terminal width and buffer length. Updated src/index.ts to handle input buffer changes and resets correctly.

eli5.text: When you type a message that gets long enough to wrap onto multiple lines above the text cursor, the on-screen text no longer leaves behind stray characters or misaligned text when you delete or edit it; instead, it smoothly clears and redraws the wrapped lines as you type. Previously, only a single line of text was handled, so wrapping input caused leftover characters and confusing cursor jumps when using backspace. This fix is already live for anyone typing multi-line input in the interface.

ai.title: Refactor CLI into modular components
ai.summary: Split monolithic index.ts into discrete modules: cli.ts, config.ts, menu.ts, and websocket-client.ts. ChatStorage now manages currentChat state with getCurrentChat/setCurrentChat methods. Backend prompts.ts fixes debug log variable scope in processFileBlock. This structure separates concerns for easier maintenance and testing.

eli5.text: The assistant's code was cleaned up so it's easier to maintain behind the scenes. The parts that handled typing, settings, menus, and connections were moved out of one big file into separate files, and the way chats are tracked was updated to keep better track of the current chat. If you looked at the files, you'd see a cleaner and more organized structure, but your experience using the assistant stays the same. This cleanup is already live.

ai.title: STOPMARKER shortened to END, claude.ts removed
ai.summary: STOP_MARKER constant in common/src/constants.ts changed from '[END_OF_RESPONSE]' to '[END]'. System prompt and continuation logic updated to encourage explicit marker usage for user guidance. Deleted unused src/claude.ts Anthropic wrapper. Removed redundant cli.promptUser() call in src/index.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes responding to you, it now signals the end with a shorter marker '[END]' instead of the longer '[END_OF_RESPONSE]' you may have noticed before. The instructions telling the assistant how and when to stop were also tightened up, so it is nudged to include that marker and you are more reliably prompted to continue if it forgets. Behind the scenes, the developers deleted the old helper file that connected to the assistant and removed a leftover line that asked for your input twice. This is a small consistency and cleanup change, so you will mainly notice the slightly shorter ending token if you were watching for the old one.
